solutions.check: 30 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 29 answers the paper printed; printed-crossing fills: 16-down

clue.text: Died with Lawrence? Rubbish!

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
T. E. Lawrence (of Arabia) enlisted in the RAF under the assumed name Ross

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a claim that a death was linked to Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Lawrence is wanted by his alias: after his Arabian fame T. E. Lawrence served in the ranks as Aircraftman Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is the scum skimmed off molten metal, hence worthless matter or rubbish.

clue.text: Putting off, in Paris, of agitation

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a ferment is a state of agitation or unrest

explanation.surface: A Parisian delays because of unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Deferment is postponement, the act of putting something off to later.

clue.text: No footballer is in debt

parts.note: O is a nought, so it stands for no or nothing
a wing is a footballer playing on the flank

explanation.surface: No footballer is left owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owing is still to be paid, so the debtor remains owing.

clue.text: Perhaps Machiavelli's school raised corps of engineers

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the corps' abbreviation is turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Machiavelli's old school is said to have brought up army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Machiavelli's' reads as 'Machiavelli is', with 'Perhaps' marking him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Machiavelli is the byword for a cunning political plotter, an example of an intriguer.

clue.text: Exemplary chap, he, at conveying information

parts.note: signal as an adjective means outstanding or exemplary, as in a signal success
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A model fellow is praised for being good at passing on news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he, at conveying information' reads as 'one who is at (engaged in) conveying information': a railway worker who operates signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway signal-box worker passes messages to train drivers by working the signals.

clue.text: Miss Page is upset by this colour

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the words Anne is upside down, reading them bottom to top

parts.note: Anne Page is the young woman in Shakespeare's The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: A young woman is distressed by a particular shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Page could be any young woman; the setter means Shakespeare's Anne Page.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthy brownish-yellow or reddish pigment named after the Italian city of Siena.

clue.text: Webster's lightweight material?

parts.note: a webster is read as one who makes webs, a spider, whose fine filmy threads are the material meant

explanation.walkthrough: Webster suggests the dictionary or the dramatist, but here it is a spider, a maker of webs.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine silky film of cobweb floating in the air, also used for any very light fabric.

clue.text: Took for granted this name was false

definitions.meaning: an alias, a false name taken on in place of one's own

explanation.surface: Someone presumed that a name was fake.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is both to suppose without proof and to take on a pseudonym as one's own.

clue.text: In which one may travel by car to demo, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of car to demo may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone could drive to a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession of motor vehicles, in which dignitaries ride.

clue.text: Prime Minister once, and not half thin!

parts.note: nor means and not

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters of the word thin

explanation.surface: An old PM is described as rather on the slim side.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782, during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North led the British government in the years America was lost.

clue.text: Strange if the lass is inconstant

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the words if the lass are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Oddly enough, the girl turns out to be fickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untrue to a lover or a promise is fickle, the sense of inconstant here.

clue.text: In Aeschylus, a Tyrian deity

indicators.note: In signals that the letters sit inside the run of words Aeschylus, a Tyrian, straddling the word breaks

explanation.surface: A god from Tyre is said to appear in a play by the Greek tragedian Aeschylus.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland spirit of Greek myth, part man and part goat, counted as a minor god.

clue.text: Noted concomitant to the progress of several companies

definitions.text: Noted concomitant to the progress of several companies

parts.words: Noted concomitant to the progress of several companies
parts.note: noted means set to musical notes, and the companies are those of soldiers in a regiment on the move, so this is a tune to march to

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' looks like 'famous', but here it means written in musical notes; 'companies' sounds commercial but means army units.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit's own parade tune played as its troops advance.

clue.text: …no sadness of farewell When I —" (Tennyson)

parts.words: no sadness of farewell When I
parts.note: a gap-fill from Tennyson's poem Crossing the Bar, where the poet hopes for no grief at his parting when he sets out to sea

explanation.walkthrough: The lines run 'And may there be no sadness of farewell, / When I embark'; the missing word is the last of the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on board a ship and set out, which in the poem stands for dying.

clue.text: Incidental result of multiplication?

parts.note: the result of multiplying numbers is called their product, read here as a secondary outcome

explanation.walkthrough: Multiplication suggests arithmetic, whose result is a product; the answer is a side result of a process.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary thing produced alongside the main output of a process.

clue.text: Sec principal touch down at Portland Bill, say

parts.note: the principal of a school is its head
an aircraft touching down is coming in to land

explanation.surface: A plane is told to land at a spot on the Dorset coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Portland Bill is a promontory on the Dorset coast of southern England; 'Bill' here is a beak of land, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory jutting out to sea is an example of a cape or point of high land.

clue.text: Nurses' applications to perform in choir in costume

indicators.note: in costume places the choral performance word within the garment word

parts.note: a costume is a dress
to perform in a choir is to sing

explanation.surface: Nurses are told to sing in the choir dressed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' does the work: SING goes inside DRESS to make DRES-SING-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandages and ointments applied to wounds by nurses.

clue.text: Airmen qualified to be in soldier's writings

indicators.note: to be in tells us the airmen and the qualified word sit inside the soldier

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the RAF is the Royal Air Force, made up of airmen
someone qualified for a job is fit for it

explanation.surface: Fit airmen are to be written about in a soldier's letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writings' is loose: the sense is scribblings on walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti are scribbled words and drawings on public walls.

clue.text: Records attempt at making a wall-covering

parts.note: records made on magnetic tape are tapes
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Someone records their first go at making wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven hanging picture traditionally hung on a wall for decoration and warmth.

clue.text: Perhaps Rosinante's back to support his handiwork

definitions.text: Perhaps Rosinante's back to support his handiwork

parts.words: Perhaps Rosinante's back to support his handiwork
parts.note: Rosinante is Don Quixote's horse, standing for any horse, whose back carries the leather seat this craftsman makes

explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like 'returns', but it is the horse's back, on which the craftsman's product rests.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes and repairs harness and riding seats for horses.

clue.text: Commit robbery and run away from the church

parts.note: to run away is to flee
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Thieves rob a church and make their getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle or strip them of money, as a sheep is shorn.

clue.text: Creature spotted by old Pope on way round Pennsylvania?

parts.note: Leo was the name of thirteen Popes
PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: An animal is seen by an elderly Pope on a road near Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' looks like 'seen', but it belongs to the definition: the creature has spots.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat known for its spotted coat.

clue.text: Henry's up and round about in Pakistan

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
O is round in shape
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Henry is up and walking around somewhere in Pakistan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Pakistan' stands for a city there; 'Henry's' is 'Henry is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is the capital of Punjab province, Pakistan's second-largest city.

clue.text: Its potential victim dreaded a haircut

definitions.text: Its potential victim dreaded a haircut

parts.words: Its potential victim dreaded a haircut
parts.note: the courtier in the Greek legend sat beneath a blade hung by a single hair, so his fear was of that hair being cut

explanation.walkthrough: A haircut here is the cutting of the one horsehair holding the weapon over the diner's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary blade dangling by a hair over a courtier at Dionysius's banquet, a symbol of ever-present peril.

clue.text: Hood's bridge of these dimensions, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word for dimensions is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: dimensions describe size

explanation.surface: A question about the measurements of a bridge in a poem by Thomas Hood.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood wrote the poem The Bridge of Sighs; the Venetian bridge gave it the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's title names the Venice bridge crossed by prisoners, who breathed deep breaths of sorrow.

clue.text: Learning about one of France's waterways

indicators.note: about means the learning word goes around the numeral

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A study of one of France's canals or rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France.

clue.text: Severe treatment finishes off the son of Gargantua

indicators.note: finishes off means only the closing part of that giant's name is used, the opening letters cut away

parts.note: in Rabelais, Gargantua's son is the giant Pantagruel

explanation.surface: A harsh regime polishes off a giant's son.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'give someone gruel' was old slang for punishing them severely.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin porridge, and by extension old slang for a harsh punishment or a beating.

clue.text: In which one is considered alone

definitions.text: In which one is considered alone

parts.words: In which one is considered alone
parts.note: a state in which a person is regarded as being by themselves, also suggesting a thing being studied on its own

explanation.definitionFit: Being set apart from others, as in solitary confinement or studying something by itself.

clue.text: Rent in USA makes us gloomy

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters of rent in USA are reworked to form a new word

explanation.surface: Paying rent in America leaves the speaker depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a sullen, morose temperament, supposedly under the planet Saturn's influence.

clue.text: 2 back-street compositions

parts.note: due is Italian for two, as in musical directions

indicators.note: back signals that the abbreviation for street is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Two pieces of music are written about a back-street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' looks like one word but splits: 'back' turns ST into TS. 'compositions' also nods to 2: these are pieces for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of music written for two performers.
